samples.text: The service is currently running on a workaround: "Manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period". The basis for that override is the confirmed cause: "Stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register". The override maps the affected codes by hand to their correct current values, so it bypasses the stale entry rather than repairing it. No planned or prior-period figure exists to set against this position. The comparison that matters is between running on the override now and waiting for a permanent correction to the register. This is a holding position, not a fix, and readers deciding whether to wait should treat it that way. The override lets the period be valued, which is what the close needs this week. It does not change the register itself, so the next run that reads the register without the override would meet the same stale mapping and fail in the same way. Teams that need valuation figures for this period can use them now. Teams

The valuation failure has one established cause: "Stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register". That was not the first explanation. Triage initially recorded the cause as "Overnight ERP outage", and the morning was spent testing that theory against the upstream system. It was ruled out on direct evidence, because "ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window". Once the outage theory fell away, the classification that followed is the finding this review rests on: "control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer". Put plainly, the stale row was not a random data error. It was the expected output of a table that nobody was accountable for and nobody was obliged to check before a change went live.
